html:
A Portuguese Jesuit priest, preacher, diplomat and writer who grew up in Brazil and became the greatest prose stylist of the Portuguese language in his century. He was born in Lisbon and taken as a child to Salvador da Bahia, where he joined the Jesuits.

His sermons made him famous. In 1640 he preached against the Dutch, who were then attacking Brazil. After Portugal broke free of Spain that year, he became an adviser and envoy of King John IV.

In the 1650s he led Jesuit missions in Maranhão and the Amazon. He spoke out hard against settlers who enslaved Indigenous people, and won laws putting the villages under Jesuit care. The settlers expelled the Jesuits in 1661. He also argued for the converted Jews of Portugal, the New Christians, and was tried and held by the Inquisition for his prophetic writings. He did not oppose African slavery, though he condemned its cruelty in his sermons. He died in Salvador in 1697.
